verses.text: Jethro, the priest of Midian and Moses' father-in-law, heard about everything God had done for Moses and for his people Israel, and how the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.
Moses had sent his wife Zipporah back home, and his father-in-law Jethro had taken her in,
along with her two sons. One son was named Gershom, because Moses had said, "I have become a foreigner in a foreign land."
The other was named Eliezer, because Moses had said, "My father's God was my helper. He saved me from Pharaoh's sword."
Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, came to Moses in the desert, together with Moses' wife and sons. Moses was camped near the mountain of God.
Jethro sent word to Moses: "I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you with your wife and her two sons."
So Moses went out to meet his father-in-law. He bowed down and kissed him. They asked how each other was, and then they went into the tent.
Moses told his father-in-law everything the LORD had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians for Israel's sake. He told him about all the troubles they had met on the way, and how the LORD had saved them.
Jethro was very happy to hear about all the good things the LORD had done for Israel in saving them from the Egyptians.
Jethro said, "Praise the LORD, who saved you from the Egyptians and from Pharaoh, and who saved the people from the power of the Egyptians.
Now I know that the LORD is greater than all other gods, because of what he did to those who treated Israel so proudly."
Then Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and other sacrifices to God. Aaron came with all the leaders of Israel to eat a meal with Moses' father-in-law in the presence of God.
The next day Moses sat down to judge the people's cases, and the people stood around him from morning until evening.

When his father-in-law saw everything Moses was doing for the people, he said, "What is this you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone as judge, while all these people stand around you from morning until evening?"
Moses answered him, "Because the people come to me to ask what God wants.
Whenever they have a problem, they come to me, and I decide between one person and another. I also teach them God's rules and laws."
Moses' father-in-law said to him, "What you are doing is not good.
You and these people who come to you will only wear yourselves out. The work is too heavy for you. You cannot do it alone.
Now listen to me, and I will give you some advice, and may God be with you. You must speak for the people in front of God and bring their problems to him.
Teach them his rules and laws. Show them how they should live and what work they should do.
But choose capable men from all the people, men who fear God, who can be trusted, and who hate taking bribes. Put them in charge of the people as leaders over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.

Let them judge the people's cases at all times. They can bring the difficult cases to you, but they can decide the simple cases themselves. That will make your load lighter, because they will share it with you.
If you do this, and God commands you to, you will be able to stand the strain. And all these people will go home satisfied."
Moses listened to his father-in-law and did everything he said.
He chose capable men from all Israel and made them leaders of the people, leaders over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
They judged the people's cases at all times. They brought the difficult cases to Moses, but they decided the simple ones themselves.
Then Moses sent his father-in-law on his way, and Jethro went back to his own country.
